title: Custom Interpreters for Fixed, Simple Validation
pattern: A local tokenizer, grammar tree, or AST interpreter implements simple, fixed format or input validation (such as postal codes, phone numbers, or basic length and character constraints) that straightforward compiled checks or standard validators already express.
why_bad: The extra language machinery increases code footprint and cognitive overhead without a corresponding expressive need: it requires maintaining a parser stack, slows validation, complicates basic error messaging, and lacks compile-time verification for rules that regular expressions or a few native checks solve in a few lines.
detection: Simple format-validation helper modules contain custom tokenizing, parsing, or AST evaluation machinery, whether for postal- or phone-shaped format checks or for basic length/character-class constraints on field values.
counterexample: `Context-dependent`. Format rules that are genuinely complex, vary dynamically at runtime based on market localization, or are defined entirely by non-programming users; general-purpose forms engines where validation logic is configured dynamically via UI schemas and a language is a real requirement.
source: [2nd] Andrew Hunt_ David Hurst Thomas - _The Pragmatic Programmer_ Your Journey to Mastery_, 20th Anniversary Edition (2019, Addison-Wesley Professional).pdf, Topic 28 "Domain Languages"; Joshua Kerievsky - _Refactoring to Patterns_ (2004, Addison-Wesley Professional).pdf, Chapter 7 "Replace Implicit Language with Interpreter".
